chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Abdullah ibn al-Munbih from Husayn ibn Alwan from Amr ibn Khalid from Zayd ibn Ali from his father from his forefathers, peace be upon them, said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'For the martyr are seven characteristics from Allah: First, with the first drop of his blood, all his sins are forgiven; Second, his head rests in the lap of his two wives from the Hur al-Ayn, and they wipe the dust from his face, saying 'Welcome,' and he says the same to them; Third, he is clothed with the garments of Paradise; Fourth, the keepers of Paradise vie with each other to take him with them, each offering a pleasant breeze; Fifth, his station is shown to him; Sixth, it is said to his soul, 'Roam in Paradise wherever you wish'; Seventh, he gazes upon the face of Allah. And indeed, this is a rest for every Prophet and Martyr.'

key_terms.يَنْظُرَ فِي وَجْهِ اللَّهِ: Gazing upon the face of Allah

ai.seo_question: What are the seven special rewards for a martyr in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the virtues of Jihad, this hadith from the progeny of Imam Ali (AS) details the seven specific divine favors bestowed upon the martyr. It emphasizes a progressive spiritual elevation, culminating in the ultimate beatific vision of Allah, which is described as the true rest for all prophets and martyrs, thereby linking the martyr's status directly to the highest echelons of Islamic spirituality.
